schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE ACTIVITY (
    USER_ID INT,
    SESSION_ID INT,
    ACTIVITY_DATE DATE,
    ACTIVITY_TYPE ENUM('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'),
    CHECK (ACTIVITY_TYPE IN ('OPEN_SESSION', 'END_SESSION', 'SCROLL_DOWN', 'SEND_MESSAGE'))
);
q1: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY , COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY DAY HAVING DATEDIFF('2019-07-27', ACTIVITY_DATE) < 30
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY, COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY WHERE ACTIVITY_DATE BETWEEN '2019-06-28' AND '2019-07-27' GROUP BY ACTIVITY_DATE
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT ACTIVITY_DATE AS DAY , COUNT(DISTINCT USER_ID) AS ACTIVE_USERS FROM ACTIVITY GROUP BY DAY HAVING DATEDIFF('2019-07-27', ACTIVITY_DATE) < 30
counterexample: INSERT INTO ACTIVITY (USER_ID, SESSION_ID, ACTIVITY_DATE, ACTIVITY_TYPE) VALUES (1, 101, '2019-06-27', 'OPEN_SESSION'), (2, 102, '2019-06-28', 'SCROLL_DOWN'), (3, 103, '2019-07-27', 'SEND_MESSAGE');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 filters the data between '2019-06-28' and '2019-07-27' and then groups by ACTIVITY_DATE, while Q2 groups by a calculated DAY (ACTIVITY_DATE) and filters based on the difference between '2019-07-27' and ACTIVITY_DATE.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 will count active users for each day between '2019-06-28' and '2019-07-27', while Q2 will count active users for each day up to 30 days before '2019-07-27' (i.e., from '2019-06-28' to '2019-07-27'), but it will not group by the actual ACTIVITY_DATE.
